*[UGC NET December 2022 S1 · Q.77]*
options: A, C, E, B, D Passage / data for Q.91-95 (December 2022 S1) Read the passage and answer the questions that follow U. Pagano and M.A. Rossi (2009) have advanced a hypothesis that states that, 'the crash of the knowledge economy is due to the intellectual monopolies, i.e. the huge protection inherent to Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs). The authors have stated - the institutions, which are facilitating IPRs are responsible for the crash. According to the authors, IPRs have acted as 'super-tariffs' as they have raised the cost of investment for countries that had neither abundant cheap labour nor high amounts of IPR resources. The IPRs may have subsequently exerted negative effect even on IP (Intellectual Property) rich firms or the conflicting rights of the firm may affect each other's investments and result in a situation of a savings glut. Therefore, the authors suggested - "if intellectual monopolies are one of the causes of the crash, the remedies should not only focus on monetary policy, financial regulation or even on standard Keynesian policies, rather regulation should be made to decrease the level of intellectual monopolization of economy". The policy measures they propose, however, aimed at redressing the balance between public and private knowledge, would not only have strong short-run super-multiplicative effects but would have long-run benefits as well.

questions.explanation: Per the passage: intellectual monopolies (IPR protection).

questions.q:
Why have the authors considered IPRs as a super tariff?  
*[UGC NET December 2022 S1 · Q.93]*
options: There is a large scale reduction in tariffs but substantial increase in some sectors, in some countries, hence it is considered as a super tariff.
After the Uruguay Round, the tariff rate has declined multiple times and that boosts economic growth, hence it is considered as a super tariff.
The reduction in tariff has benefited the developed countries, hence it is called a super tariff.
The IPRs have raised the cost of investments for countries that had neither abundant cheap labour nor high amount of IPR resources, hence it acted as a super tariff.
questions.explanation: They raised investment costs for countries without cheap labour or IPR resources.

questions.q:
How are the IPRs responsible for a savings glut?  
*[UGC NET December 2022 S1 · Q.94]*
options: IPR has lead to economic growth, which has led to a savings glut.
The aggregate demand has fallen substantially and that has led to the savings glut.
The IPRs have given rise to conflicting rights for different firms, which has affected the volume of investment negatively and resulted in a situation of a savings glut.
The IPRs have led to poverty and that has led to a savings glut.
questions.explanation: Conflicting rights depress investment, giving a savings glut.
